title: Probability
subtitle: Chance, Outcomes & Compound Events
bounds: PROTOCOL §4b fractions. Every probability in a prompt or a correct answer is a fraction a/b in simplest form with b 2-12 (numerator at most 12; at most 12 equally likely outcomes, a die and a coin being 12), or a decimal or percent of the §4b kind (at most 2 places and 2 non-zero digits; 10, 20, 25, 50, 75 percent and tens of percent). T1 range questions also show values past 1 (up to 300 percent, or 3) because that is the concept. No two-dice probabilities (1/36). Counts are whole numbers 1-100 from times-table facts: outcome counts multiply factors 2-10 (three stages: the two smaller factors multiply to 10 or less; at most 4 coin flips); predictions are n ÷ d = k with d 2-10 and k 2-10, then k × a (a 1-9); a sample of 4-25 kids scales by a factor 2-10 to a group of 100 or less; an estimate divides both numbers by a factor 2-10 (totals up to 50). A product of two chances has a denominator of 12 or less (coin and die) or is a square of 2 or 3 (two draws with replacement). Wrong choices may be any size up to 999 and may be improper. Choices use one form per item and never repeat a value.

tiers.name: How Likely?
tiers.description: Place chances on the 0 to 1 scale, from impossible to certain.

tiers.name: Simple Probability
tiers.description: Favorable outcomes over all outcomes, in simplest form.

tiers.name: Complement & Predict
tiers.description: The chance of not, expected counts, and predicting from a sample.

tiers.name: Sample Spaces
tiers.description: Count the outcomes of two- and three-stage events.

tiers.name: Compound Events
tiers.description: The chance of two or more events happening together.

SCALE_FLIP.student: Closer to 1 means MORE likely. 0 is impossible, 1 is certain.
SCALE_FLIP.teacher: Reverses the 0-to-1 scale: reads a large probability as unlikely, or 0 as certain.

HALF_WORD.student: Only 1/2 is equally likely. Near 1 is likely, near 0 is unlikely.

ROUNDED.student: Certain means exactly 1 and impossible exactly 0. Close is just likely.
ROUNDED.teacher: Rounds a probability near 1 up to certain, or near 0 down to impossible.

WORD_MIXUP.student: 0 is impossible, 1 is certain, 1/2 is the middle. Place the number first.
WORD_MIXUP.teacher: Picks a likelihood word that does not match where the number sits on the scale.

HALF_LEANS.student: 1/2 is the middle of the scale: neither likely nor unlikely.
HALF_LEANS.teacher: Reads a probability of exactly 1/2 as leaning likely or unlikely.

OVER_ONE.student: A probability is never more than 1. Even a sure thing is just 1.
OVER_ONE.teacher: Accepts a value above 1 (or 100%) as a probability.

NEGATIVE.student: A probability is never below 0. Impossible is 0, the lowest it goes.
NEGATIVE.teacher: Accepts a negative number as a probability.

EDGE_EXCLUDED.student: 0 and 1 ARE probabilities: impossible and certain events.
EDGE_EXCLUDED.teacher: Thinks 0 and 1 are not allowed as probabilities.

RANGE_CHECK.student: A probability is 0 to 1 (0% to 100%). Look for the one outside that.
RANGE_CHECK.teacher: Picks a value that is inside 0 to 1 when asked for one outside it.

PERCENT_MIX.student: As a number it stops at 1. The 100 belongs to the percent, 100%.
PERCENT_MIX.teacher: Mixes the percent scale (0-100) with the 0-to-1 scale.

PART_TO_PART.student: Probability is part out of the WHOLE, not part out of the other part.
PART_TO_PART.teacher: Compares favorable to unfavorable outcomes (odds) instead of favorable to all.

OTHER_EVENT.student: That is the opposite event. Find the one the question asks about.
OTHER_EVENT.teacher: Answers for the complementary event (or its count) instead of the asked event.

ONE_OVER_TOTAL.student: Count every outcome that fits, not just one: favorable over total.
ONE_OVER_TOTAL.teacher: Uses 1 over the total, as if only one outcome were favorable.

EQUAL_CHANCE.student: Outcomes are not always 50-50 or equal. Count favorable over total.
EQUAL_CHANCE.teacher: Assumes equal chances (1/2, or 1 over the number of colors) without counting.

BOUNDARY.student: Check the edge: 'more than 4' leaves out 4, 'at least 5' keeps 5.
BOUNDARY.teacher: Off by one at the boundary of 'more than', 'less than', 'at least' or 'at most'.

PRIME_ONE.student: 1 is not prime: a prime has exactly two factors, like 2, 3 and 5.

DISTINCT_OUTCOMES.student: Repeats count: three A's are three outcomes, not one.
DISTINCT_OUTCOMES.teacher: Counts each different letter once, ignoring how many times it appears.

SAME_AS_EVENT.student: That is the chance of the event itself. 'Not' asks for the rest.
SAME_AS_EVENT.teacher: Gives P(event) when asked for P(not event).

ADD_TO_ONE.student: P(not A) = 1 minus P(A). Subtract from 1; a chance never tops 1.
ADD_TO_ONE.teacher: Adds the chance to 1 instead of subtracting it from 1.

ONE_OTHER.student: 'Not red' means ALL the other colors together, not just one.
ONE_OTHER.teacher: Counts only one of the other colors for the complement.

IGNORED_NUMERATOR.student: Use the whole fraction: 3/10 of 20 is 3 tenths, not 1 tenth.
IGNORED_NUMERATOR.teacher: Divides by the denominator but forgets to multiply by the numerator.

INVERTED_P.student: Multiply the tries by the chance: 1/4 of 40 is 40 ÷ 4 = 10, not 40 ÷ 1/4.
INVERTED_P.teacher: Divides the number of tries by the chance (multiplies by the denominator) instead of multiplying.

SAMPLE_COUNT.student: Scale the sample up to the whole group; the sample count is too small.
SAMPLE_COUNT.teacher: Reports the count found in the sample as the prediction for the population.

ADDITIVE.student: Scale by multiplying: the same fraction of a bigger group, not adding on.
ADDITIVE.teacher: Adds the difference in group sizes instead of scaling proportionally.

SCALE_ONLY.student: That is only the scale factor. Multiply it by the count in the sample.
SCALE_ONLY.teacher: Stops after finding the scale factor (population ÷ sample).

FLIPPED.student: Chance = successes over tries, with the successes on top.
FLIPPED.teacher: Writes the ratio upside down (tries over successes).

ADDED_COUNTS.student: Pair every choice with every other: multiply the counts, don't add.
ADDED_COUNTS.teacher: Adds the numbers of choices instead of multiplying (counting principle).

ONE_STAGE.student: Count both stages: each outcome of one pairs with each of the other.
ONE_STAGE.teacher: Counts the outcomes of only one stage.

FORGOT_ONE.student: Every stage multiplies the count. Don't skip one.
FORGOT_ONE.teacher: Multiplies only two of the three stages.

MIXED_OPS.teacher: Adds some stages and multiplies others.

ORDER_BLIND.student: HT and TH are different outcomes. Order counts, so count both.
ORDER_BLIND.teacher: Treats outcomes that differ only in order as one (counts head totals, not sequences).

MULT_BY_COUNT.student: Each flip doubles the count: 2 × 2 × 2 for three flips, not 2 × 3.
MULT_BY_COUNT.teacher: Multiplies outcomes per trial by the number of trials.

POWER_FLIP.student: Two outcomes per flip, once per flip: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, not 3 × 3.
POWER_FLIP.teacher: Swaps base and exponent: flips squared instead of 2 to the number of flips.

COUNTED_ALL.student: That counts every outcome. Count only the ones that fit the event.
COUNTED_ALL.teacher: Gives the size of the whole sample space instead of the event.

ONE_OUTCOME.student: Count ALL the outcomes that fit the event, not just one of them.
ONE_OUTCOME.teacher: Treats the event as a single outcome.

IGNORED_PART.student: Both conditions must hold: heads AND even, not just one of them.
IGNORED_PART.teacher: Counts outcomes meeting only one of the two conditions.

TOTAL_NOT_EVENT.student: That is every outcome. Count only the ones that fit.
TOTAL_NOT_EVENT.teacher: Gives the whole sample space size.

NOT_PAIRED.student: Pair them up: each coin side goes with each number (H1, H2, T1, T2).
NOT_PAIRED.teacher: Lists the parts of each stage separately instead of the combined outcomes.

MISSED_ONE.student: List every pairing: each coin side with each number. Check for gaps.
MISSED_ONE.teacher: Gives an incomplete list of the sample space.

MATCHING_ONLY.student: List every outcome, not only the matching ones. HT and TH count too.
MATCHING_ONLY.teacher: Lists only the outcomes where both parts match.

ADDED_PROBS.student: For 'and', multiply the chances. Adding makes a chance that's too big.
ADDED_PROBS.teacher: Adds the probabilities of the two events instead of multiplying.

ADD_DENOMS.teacher: Adds the denominators (or the denominators and not the numerators) when multiplying.

FORGOT_STAGE.student: Both parts must happen. Multiply by the other part's chance too.
FORGOT_STAGE.teacher: Gives the chance of only one stage of a compound event.

ONE_ORDER.student: Either order works (red then blue, or blue then red): count both.
ONE_ORDER.teacher: Counts only one of the orders when either order satisfies the event.

ORDER_OVER.student: The order is given: 'red then blue' is one order only. Don't double it.
ORDER_OVER.teacher: Doubles for two orders when the event names a single order.
